acerbi: acerbus, -a, -um — bitter, harsh; n. as noun, bitterness (n. gen. sg., partitive: quidquid acerbi, 'whatever of bitter')
actu: āctus, -ūs (m.) — driving, impulse, momentum (abl. sg., magnō actū, 'with great force')
aequato: aequō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to make level, balance (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg., in abl. abs. with exāmine)
alitur: aliter (adv.) — otherwise, in another way (the print's 'alitur' is a misprint for aliter; nōn aliter, 'not otherwise')
appenninus: Appenninus (Apenninus), -ī (m.) — the Apennines, Italy's mountain range, here called father (nom. sg.)
armosque: armus, -ī (m.) — shoulder, upper foreleg (of animals) (acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
aspexit: aspiciō, -ere, -spexī, -spectum — to look at, behold, catch sight of (3rd sg. perf.)
athos: Athos, -ī (m.) — Athos, the great mountain of northern Greece (nom. sg., Greek form)
avulsum: āvellō, -ere, -vellī (-vulsī), -vulsum — to tear away, wrench off (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg., with saxum)
cessere: cēdō, -ere, cessī, cessum — to withdraw, give way, yield (3rd pl. perf. = cessērunt)
coiisse: coeō, -īre, -iī (-īvī), -itum — to come together, meet (perf. inf. = coīsse, spelt coiisse)
compactis: compingō, -ere, -pēgī, -pāctum — to fasten together, join (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl., with trabibus)
confusus: confundō, -ere, -fūdī, -fūsum — to pour together, confound, bewilder (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
congeminant: congeminō, -āre — to redouble, double (3rd pl. pres.)
coniectis: coniciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to throw, hurl (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl., with hastīs, in abl. abs.)
conscendebat: cōnscendō, -ere, -scendī, -scēnsum — to climb aboard, mount (3rd sg. impf.)
conversis: convertō, -ere, -vertī, -versum — to turn round, turn (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl., with frontibus)
crebros: creber, -bra, -brum — thick, frequent, repeated (m. acc. pl., with ictūs)
damnet: damnō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to condemn, doom (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
daturum: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give; exscidiō dare, to give to destruction (fut. act. part., m. acc. sg., fut. inf. with esse and sē understood)
daunius: Daunius, -a, -um — of Daunus, Daunian (m. nom. sg., with hērōs; of Turnus, son of Daunus)
deiecturum: dēiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to throw down, cast down (fut. act. part., m. acc. sg., fut. inf. with esse and sē understood)
deposuere: dēpōnō, -ere, -posuī, -positum — to lay down, set aside (3rd pl. perf. = dēposuērunt)
discessere: discēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to withdraw, depart, part (3rd pl. perf. = discessērunt)
discussae: discutiō, -ere, -cussī, -cussum — to shake apart, scatter, dispel (perf. pass. part., f. nom. pl., with umbrae)
dissiluit: dissiliō, -īre, -siluī — to leap apart, burst asunder, shatter (3rd sg. perf.)
duas: duo, duae, duo — two (f. acc. pl., with lances)
eduxerat: ēdūcō, -ere, -dūxī, -ductum — to lead out; raise up, build high (3rd sg. plupf.)
eque: ex, ē (prep. + abl.) — out of, from + -que 'and' (eque rotis, 'and from the wheels')
examine: exāmen, -inis (n.) — tongue of a balance, needle of the scales; also a swarm (abl. sg.)
exclamant: exclāmō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to cry out, shout aloud (3rd pl. pres.)
exscidioque: exscidium (excidium), -ī (n.) — destruction, ruin (dat. sg., of goal: exscidiō dare) + -que 'and'
exsultatque: exsultō, -āre — to leap up, bound, exult (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
flectat: flectō, -ere, flēxī, flexum — to bend, turn; sē flectere, to turn oneself (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
fulminat: fulminō, -āre — to flash lightning, hurl thunderbolts; blaze like lightning (3rd sg. pres.)
furere: furō, -ere, -uī — to rage, be mad, rave (pres. inf.; sine me furere, 'let me rage')
genitos: gignō, -ere, genuī, genitum — to beget, bear; genitus, born (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with virōs)
horrendumque: horrendus, -a, -um — dreadful, terrible (n. acc. sg. used as adv., 'terribly') + -que 'and'
imperitet: imperitō, -āre — to rule, command (+ dat.) (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
implorans: implōrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to beg, entreat, call upon (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
infigunt: infīgō, -ere, -fīxī, -fīxum — to fix in, drive in, plant (3rd pl. pres.)
inhibete: inhibeō, -ēre, -uī, -itum — to hold back, check, restrain (2nd pl. imper.)
instraverat: īnsternō, -ere, -strāvī, -strātum — to lay over, spread upon, floor (3rd sg. plupf.)
iunctos: iungō, -ere, iūnxī, iūnctum — to join, yoke (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with equōs)
lances: lānx, lancis (f.) — dish; pan of a balance (acc. pl.)
luere: luō, -ere, luī — to pay, pay off; atone for (a penalty) (pres. inf.; foedus luere, to atone for the treaty)
madet: madeō, -ēre, maduī — to be wet, drip, be soaked (3rd sg. pres.)
mussantque: mussō, -āre — to murmur, mutter; hesitate silently (3rd pl. pres.) + -que 'and'
mussat: mussō, -āre — to murmur, mutter; hesitate silently (3rd sg. pres.)
mutum: mūtus, -a, -um — dumb, silent, speechless (n. nom. sg., with pecus)
nemori: nemus, nemoris (n.) — grove, wood, pasture (dat. sg., with imperitet)
palantia: palor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to wander, straggle, scatter (pres. part., n. acc. pl., with terga)
parcite: parcō, -ere, pepercī — to spare, show mercy; refrain, hold off (+ dat.) (2nd pl. imper.)
patuerunt: pateō, -ēre, patuī — to lie open, stand open, stretch out (3rd pl. perf.)
praecipitatque: praecipitō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to throw headlong; cut short, hurry (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
pulsabant: pulsō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to beat, batter, strike (3rd pl. impf.)
resplendent: resplendeō, -ēre — to shine back, gleam, glitter (3rd pl. pres.)
ruitque: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
saces: Saces, -is (m.) — Saces, a Rutulian on Turnus's side who brings him the news from the city (nom. sg.)
saltum: saltus, -ūs (m.) — leap, bound (acc. sg.; saltum dare, to leap)
significatque: significō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to make a sign, signal (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
sila: Sīla, -ae (f.) — Sila, the great forested mountain range of Bruttium in south Italy (abl. sg.)
sonoro: sonōrus, -a, -um — resounding, ringing, loud (n. abl. sg., with aere)
strictisque: stringō, -ere, strīnxī, strictum — to draw (a blade), strip (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl., with mucrōnibus) + -que 'and'
subdideratque: subdō, -ere, -didī, -ditum — to put under, set beneath (3rd sg. plupf.) + -que 'and'
subeat: subeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to come up, come to the rescue, approach (3rd sg. pres. subj., in a ni-clause)
suffecit: sufficiō, -ere, -fēcī, -fectum — to suffice, be enough, serve (3rd sg. perf.)
summove: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost (m./n. abl. sg., with Taburnō) + -ve 'or'
sustentant: sustentō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to hold up, sustain, hold out (3rd pl. pres.)
taburno: Taburnus, -ī (m.) — Taburnus, a mountain in Samnium (abl. sg.)
trepidique: trepidus, -a, -um — anxious, alarmed, trembling (m. nom. pl., with Latīnī) + -que 'and'
undabat: undō, -āre — to surge, rise in waves, billow (3rd sg. impf.)
varia: varius, -a, -um — varied, many-sided, changing (f. abl. sg., with imāgine)
ventumst: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (impersonal perf. pass., ventum est, 'one came'; est elided)
vergat: vergō, -ere — to incline, tip, sink (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
verius: vērus, -a, -um — true, right; vērius, more rightly (comp., n. nom. sg., predicate with est understood)

__broaden__.fidissima: fīdus, -a, -um — faithful, trusty; fīdissima, most faithful (superl., f. voc. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (rēgīna, tuī fīdissima, 'most faithful to you')
__broaden__.futilis: fūtilis, -e — worthless, empty, untrustworthy (m. nom. sg., with auctor; non futilis, 'of real weight') · also f. nom. sg. (glaciēs … fūtilis, 'brittle ice')
__broaden__.laetitia: laetitia, -ae (f.) — joy, gladness (nom. sg.) · also abl. sg. (laetitiā exsultāns, 'with joy')
__broaden__.orbis: orbis, orbis (m.) — circle, ring, round; orbis terrārum, the world (nom. sg.; acc. pl., -is for -ēs) · also gen. sg. (partibus orbis, 'of the world')
__broaden__.spumante: spūmō (1), -āre — to foam; spūmante, foaming (pres. part., n. abl. sg.) · also m. abl. sg. (equō spūmante)
__broaden__.versas: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, turn round (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., with puppēs) · also 2nd sg. pres. (currum versās, 'you turn')
__broaden__.cernere: cernō, -ere, crēvī, crētum — to discern, perceive, see (pres. inf.) · also to decide (cernere ferrō, 'to decide by the sword')
__broaden__.praeceps: praeceps, -cipitis — headlong, steep (m./f. nom. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (saxum … praeceps, a rock hurtling down)
